data.title: Carousel
data.tagline: Show several panels one at a time in the same space
data.description: A carousel often appears in promotional banners and onboarding, but later slides are easy to miss. Do not place essential information only inside it. If it moves automatically, let people pause it and provide clear controls and position indicators.

use: A small set of promotional visuals
Several related stories in one reserved area
avoid: Hide critical content on a later slide
Rotate so quickly that people cannot read
Use many slides when a list would be easier to scan

lessonPractice.title: A mobile product page shows five angles in one main-image area. Users need their current position and manual control. How should it work?

options.label: Use a carousel with previous and next controls, position, and selectable thumbnails
options.feedback: Rotating related images in one area saves narrow-screen space, while position and controls keep users in charge.

options.label: Change images every two seconds with no pause, arrows, or position
options.feedback: Users cannot hold an image for inspection, know how many remain, or return to the previous one.

options.label: Stack all five full-size images vertically and require scrolling through them
options.feedback: Every image is visible, but the mobile page becomes unnecessarily long and loses the intended single-image area.

data.agentPrompt: Build mobile product images as a user-controlled carousel with position, previous and next controls, thumbnails, swipe, and keyboard support. Do not autoplay by default. Test first and last boundaries, failed images, and a single-image product.
